comment: Deliberate breakages of rules the release gates claim to enforce.
Each entry names the gate that must fail when the rule is removed.
Run with: python tools/mutate.py
`find` must appear exactly once in `file`; if it does not, the mutation
reports NOT_APPLIED rather than passing, because a manifest that has
drifted from the code tests nothing.
`expect_gate` is matched as a substring of the failing test's full name, so
it may name a distinctive fragment — but it should name the whole gate,
because a fragment can be a prefix of a second gate and then either one
satisfies the entry. Three runner defects used to force shortened values
here and are now fixed: names were cut at the first apostrophe, output was
decoded with the console codepage (so `gate: every kind × terminal cell`
could never match), and files were restored through `Path.write_text`,
which rewrote LF as CRLF. That last one was the worst of the three: with
`*.zig text eol=lf` in `.gitattributes`, `git diff` normalises CRLF away
and shows nothing, while `cmd_job.zig`'s adjacency gate reads its own
source and ends a function body at "\n}\n" — so a corrupted tree failed
that gate under the *next* mutation's name. The runner now restores by
bytes and verifies the restored file against what it read, aborting the
run if it differs.
Deleted entry, recorded so nobody reads its absence as the rule lapsing:
`v11-live-dest-unique` mutation-tested the UNIQUE on
`idx_checkpoints_live_dest` (src/core/store/migrate.zig:511), the index
that keeps two in-flight transfers off one destination. That is no longer
a gate's job. `migrate.frozenStatement` (src/core/store/migrate.zig:621)
slices the statement out of the v11 migration text at comptime — a
`std.mem.indexOf` for the literal `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX
idx_checkpoints_live_dest`, `orelse @compileError` — on behalf of
`checkpoints_index_ddl` (src/core/store/migrate.zig:651). So weakening or
removing the index stops the build. Verified rather than assumed: dropping
`UNIQUE` from line 511 reports `no frozen statement starts with: CREATE
UNIQUE INDEX idx_checkpoints_live_dest` at migrate.zig:628, referenced
from the schema-shape drift gate. A rule the compiler refuses is stronger
than one a test catches, and a mutation that cannot compile proves nothing
about a gate either way — so the entry was deleted, not repaired. (It had
also become unrunnable for a second reason: its `find` text now appears
twice in migrate.zig, once in the DDL and once in the `frozenStatement`
call that pins it, which is why it reported NOT_APPLIED rather than
BUILD_ERROR.)

mutations.rule: `--restart` never consumes the argument after it. A flag missing from `bool_flags` is not a compile error: written last it fails with "a flag is missing its value", and written before `--json` it eats it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every boolean flag this command takes is registered, so none swallows the next argument

mutations.rule: skill/SKILL.md's published exit code for each transfer verdict is the one the binary really exits with. A number in prose that no gate reads is how the survived-kill bullet came to publish 75 for a branch that exits 1.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: SKILL.md publishes an exit code for every transfer outcome, and it is the one we exit with

mutations.rule: skill/SKILL.md's count of the verdicts `--restart` can release is held against `State.isSupersedable`, so the document cannot tell an agent to restart a transfer the statement will refuse.
mutations.find: It releases **5** of the nine verdicts above:
mutations.replace: It releases **6** of the nine verdicts above:
mutations.expect_gate: gate: SKILL.md publishes how many transfer verdicts --restart can release

mutations.rule: `--resume` never consumes the argument after it. The sibling of `M3.2-restart-not-a-bool-flag`, and the second time this exact omission would have shipped: a flag missing from `bool_flags` is not a compile error and no helper-level gate sees it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every boolean flag this command takes is registered, so none swallows the next argument

mutations.rule: The hasher a resume continues from is snapshotted at exactly the confirmed offset. Taken at a buffer boundary instead, every prefix digest a resumed transfer writes describes a range nobody can re-derive.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a hasher snapshotted at a mark, continued, equals hashing the whole file

mutations.rule: A resuming push must not truncate the remote staging partial. `beginRemoteFile` opens with `: >`, which is right for a fresh push and throws away every confirmed byte on a resume.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a resuming push appends from the offset and does not truncate the remote partial

mutations.rule: A resuming pull opens its staging partial without truncating. Truncating loses the confirmed prefix the resume was licensed to splice onto.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an interrupted pull, resumed, is byte-identical to one that was never interrupted

mutations.rule: A resuming pull writes at the confirmed offset, not at the head of the file. Writing from zero overwrites the prefix it just proved and publishes a file whose head is its own tail.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an interrupted pull, resumed, is byte-identical to one that was never interrupted

mutations.rule: A resuming push refuses a remote partial that is not the length it was licensed for. Appending to a different length splices at the wrong offset, and the digests only disagree after the whole file has moved.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a resuming push appends from the offset and does not truncate the remote partial

mutations.rule: The cut that discards a partial's unconfirmed tail reads the length back. A `dd` that did nothing is indistinguishable from one that worked until the next append lands in the wrong place.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the host's readings a push's resume rests on

mutations.rule: At offset zero there is no prefix to prove. The host will hash an empty stream and return a perfectly valid digest of nothing; offering it as a prefix proof lets a resume "prove" a prefix it never read.
mutations.find: .prefix_sha256 = if (prefix_len == 0) null else try parseDigest(arena, digest_line),
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the host's readings a push's resume rests on

mutations.rule: A hand-over moves a checkpoint's owner and nothing else. The digest declared before the first byte has to survive it, because that digest is the only thing a resumed transfer can be judged against — a resume may not re-declare one.
mutations.find:
\\UPDATE transfer_checkpoints
        \\   SET request_id = ?1, updated_at = ?2
        \\ WHERE id = ?3
mutations.replace:
\\UPDATE transfer_checkpoints
        \\   SET request_id = ?1, updated_at = ?2, expected_sha256 = NULL
        \\ WHERE id = ?3
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an interrupted pull, resumed, is byte-identical to one that was never interrupted

mutations.rule: The staged prefix is proven by its digest, not by its length. Two digests of the same length are the same length; a partial of exactly the right size can be a different file, a half-written retry, or another writer's work.
mutations.find:
if (!std.mem.eql(u8, recorded, observed))
            return .{ .partial_mismatch = "the staging partial's content does not match the checkpoint" };
mutations.replace:
if (recorded.len != observed.len)
            return .{ .partial_mismatch = "the staging partial's content does not match the checkpoint" };
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a resume refuses a changed source and a wrong partial as different facts, and moves nothing

mutations.rule: A hand-over may only take over a checkpoint that can be continued as its row describes it. Widened to everything that holds a destination, `--resume` would adopt a settled failure and splice onto a partial that failure already declared untrustworthy.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: --resume reaches exactly the adoptable states, and the statement refuses the rest

mutations.rule: Every holder state gets at most one verb, and the two sets are disjoint. A message that offers `--restart` for a state supersession refuses sends half its readers to a statement that turns them away.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: --restart and --resume divide the driver's outcomes, and neither reaches the other's

mutations.rule: skill/SKILL.md says a resume is exec-only. An agent told otherwise reads the `--via scp --resume` refusal as a bug and works around it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: SKILL.md tells an agent the two things about --resume that are load-bearing

mutations.rule: An occupied destination is a fact about the operator's data and must never be reported as a filesystem that cannot do the job.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a real local collision refuses and the existing destination is byte-for-byte unchanged

mutations.rule: A local publish asked not to replace must use the non-replacing primitive; the flag decides which rename runs.
mutations.find: if (!no_clobber) return cwd.rename(partial_path, cwd, dest_path, io);
mutations.replace: if (no_clobber) return cwd.rename(partial_path, cwd, dest_path, io);
mutations.expect_gate: gate: two local publishes race for one destination and exactly one wins

mutations.rule: A no-clobber push publishes with `ln`, never with a form of `mv`: `mv` replaces, and `mv -n` is a check followed by a rename.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a no-clobber push links rather than renames, and tells a taken name from a host that cannot link

mutations.rule: `[ -e ]` follows symlinks, so a dangling one at the destination is a name `ln` refuses and `-e` alone calls absent; `-L` is what stops that being reported as a host that cannot link.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a no-clobber push links rather than renames, and tells a taken name from a host that cannot link

mutations.rule: The host's two answers mean opposite things: 47 is the destination, 48 is the mechanism, and swapping them lies about the operator's data in both directions.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a no-clobber push links rather than renames, and tells a taken name from a host that cannot link

mutations.rule: The no-clobber promise is recorded on the checkpoint, because that is what makes it survive a process boundary and bind a later resume.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the no-clobber promise is written once and no later write can change it

mutations.rule: A boolean flag missing from `args.bool_flags` is not a compile error and silently eats the argument after it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every boolean flag this command takes is registered, so none swallows the next argument

mutations.rule: A clobber conflict and a failed rename are different findings, so they may not publish the same `proves` sentence.
mutations.find: .failed_clobber_conflict => "--no-clobber was asked for and something already occupies the destination; nothing was linked and the destination holds exactly what it held",
mutations.replace: .failed_clobber_conflict => "the rename reported failure; nothing was renamed",
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the two no-clobber refusals reach different checkpoint states

mutations.rule: The agent-facing document has to say that the two no-clobber refusals are different facts, because an agent told only 'it failed' retries a conflict into the same conflict.
mutations.find: Two refusals, and they are **different facts**. Do not treat them as one:
mutations.replace: Two refusals. Do not treat them as one:
mutations.expect_gate: gate: SKILL.md tells an agent what --no-clobber refuses and what it does not

mutations.rule: A boolean flag missing from `args.bool_flags` is not a compile error and silently eats the argument after it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every boolean flag exec takes is registered, so none swallows the next argument

mutations.rule: A channel that accepts zero bytes has failed; it is not a reason to offer the same bytes again, and it is not a completed send.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a channel that accepts nothing fails instead of being offered the same bytes forever

mutations.rule: The digest on the receipt is of the bytes the channel accepted, not of the bytes that were offered to it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a short write is normal traffic and the rest is offered again

mutations.rule: The remote is told the input has ended; without the marker its process reads a channel that never closes.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every byte value survives the input channel unchanged

mutations.rule: The terminal receipt of a run that was fed local bytes records how many the channel accepted and their SHA-256. Dropping the field to its default makes a fed run indistinguishable from one that read nothing, which is the difference the two always-null columns exist to record.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the terminal receipt records the bytes the channel accepted and their digest

mutations.rule: Command text read from `--stdin`/`--cmd-file` is sent as it was read; only `--normalize-lf` rewrites its line endings.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the command keeps its carriage returns unless normalization is asked for

mutations.rule: A stream over the ceiling renders as its head *and* its tail. Returning the head alone loses the exit-marker line the supervisor puts last, so every large-output command settles `indeterminate` — a command whose status was never in doubt reported as unknown.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a command far larger than the output ceiling still reports its own exit code

mutations.rule: The retained rendering is a constant-size allocation. A cost proportional to the output — even a thousandth of it — is the unbounded drain this ceiling replaced wearing a smaller constant: it fits any budget twice over and still grows without limit.
mutations.find: const out = try arena.alloc(u8, self.head.items.len + gap_line_max + self.ring_len);
mutations.replace: const out = try arena.alloc(u8, self.head.items.len + gap_line_max + self.ring_len + @as(usize, @intCast(self.total / 1000)));
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the output ceiling's peak allocation does not grow with the output

mutations.rule: `Passed.bytes` counts every byte off the channel, not the last read. A count that described only part of the stream would make a 10 GiB run and a 1 MiB run indistinguishable on the receipt.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the output ceiling keeps both ends at the boundary and drops only above it

mutations.rule: The digest is taken over the whole stream including the middle nobody was given. A digest of only part of it cannot be checked against a full copy fetched later, which is the entire reason a truncated run is still auditable.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the output ceiling keeps both ends at the boundary and drops only above it

mutations.rule: The gap marker is written when bytes were dropped and never when they were not. Its absence is what makes its presence mean something: an agent parsing a stdout whose middle silently vanished draws a wrong conclusion and never learns that it did.
mutations.find: const gap: []const u8 = if (self.dropped == 0) "" else self.gapLine(&gap_buf);
mutations.replace: const gap: []const u8 = if (self.dropped != 0) "" else self.gapLine(&gap_buf);
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the output ceiling keeps both ends at the boundary and drops only above it

mutations.rule: A read at least as large as the ring leaves its *last* `ring.len` bytes behind, not its first. Keeping the front of it puts the middle of the stream where the end belongs, so the exit marker is gone while `truncated` still reports the truth.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the tail ring returns the last bytes of the stream whatever the read boundaries were

mutations.rule: `stdout_bytes` is the total that came off the channel. `observed.stdout.len` — the marker-stripped length — was recorded here, and under a ceiling it is none of the numbers a reader could want: not the total, not the retained amount, and not a prefix of either.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a run under the output ceiling is unchanged and its receipt says nothing was dropped

mutations.rule: The receipt says whether the middle of a stream was dropped. A column reading `false` on a truncated run is the pseudo-success this slice exists to prevent: the caller has partial output and a ledger telling it the output is complete.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a command far larger than the output ceiling still reports its own exit code

mutations.rule: The floor under the ceiling's tail is the widest exit-marker line the supervisor can print — a `u64` nonce and the widest exit status. A bound computed from narrower arguments would let the tail shrink below a line it must always hold whole.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the output ceiling's tail cannot lose the exit marker

mutations.rule: The human notice names which stream lost its middle. Reporting both when only one was cut tells an operator that stderr is incomplete when it is whole, which is the same class of wrong answer in the other direction.
mutations.find: const which: []const u8 = if (retained.stdout.truncated and retained.stderr.truncated)
mutations.replace: const which: []const u8 = if (retained.stdout.truncated or retained.stderr.truncated)
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the truncation notice appears exactly when something was dropped

mutations.rule: A `sync` whose audit row could not be written is not a `sync` that gets to report `ok: true`. cli.zig states the rule above `receiptFatal` and names this exact call as the one that used to break it; `receiptFatal` itself does not fit a verb with no operation row, so the route is `auditFatal` - same rule, same exit 76, no invented request id.
mutations.find: }, ctx.now) catch |err| Cli.auditFatal("sync", server_name, detail, err);
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the audit write is routed, not swallowed

mutations.rule: The cascade volume that decides whether `server rm` demands --force is summed from `CascadeCounts`'s own fields. A hand-written sum is the one link of this chain nothing holds: an eighth cascading table moves the schema gate, the declaration, the field and the assignment, and the sum goes on adding seven - so a server whose only rows are in the eighth table totals zero and is deleted with no prompt and no sentence naming it.
mutations.replace: sum = counts.sessions + counts.memories + counts.jobs + counts.facts + counts.history + counts.leases + counts.redaction_rules;
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the cascade total counts every field

mutations.rule: Every reading the probe took reaches the receipt, not a placeholder. `not_requested` means `this settlement deliberately did not look`; a settlement that looked and found a foreign or unparseable document at this request's own address must say so, because the verdict can be sound while the anomaly is still a fact about the host.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the proved settlement records what it read at the result-record address

mutations.rule: `parser_carry` holds the bytes a probe held back because a `__TERMINUS_PROGRESS__` marker straddled its read window, and the next probe is the only thing that could ever use them. Written unconditionally it is destroyed on every `job status` and every `job read`, because the one production caller does not set it and binds the struct default null.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a second probe does not erase the carry the first one held back

mutations.rule: `job kill` and `job rm` publish one `status` word for `the row names no attempt`, and skill/SKILL.md defines it as `unknown`. The two verbs used to spell it at separate call sites and disagreed - `job rm` said `unchanged`, a word the document listed and never defined - so an agent branching on the documented word missed `job rm` in silence.
mutations.find: const a = attempt orelse return job_status.unknown;
mutations.expect_gate: gate: both destructive verbs answer a row with no attempt with the documented word

mutations.rule: `settleProvableBlocker` is the fifth job-settlement path and the only one with no exhaustive switch of its own to break, so a hand-built `TerminalExtra` here drops the sidecar reading with nothing failing to compile. It builds its extra through `provenSettlementExtra`, which takes the whole probe so there is no argument list the reading can be left out of.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the fifth settlement path builds its receipt extra through the shared one

mutations.rule: Every PhaseStatus variant must be produced by fromOperation; a status nobody can construct is a second vocabulary, and this module just lost two of those to deletion.
mutations.expect_gate: PhaseStatus is exactly the image of fromOperation

mutations.rule: A builtin secret header's value must never reach the audit record in clear. redactSecrets is the sole redactor for the operations ledger's argv_redacted at five call sites, so a header it cannot see is a credential in the append-only record.
mutations.expect_gate: every builtin secret name is masked by the production redactor

mutations.rule: The redaction fast path must trigger on every declared secret name, or the scan that would mask it never runs. A header whose value contains none of the old trigger words returns early and is stored in the clear.
mutations.expect_gate: every builtin secret name is masked by the production redactor
